title: Podcast Platform
description: Design a podcast platform supporting show subscriptions, episode downloads, playback position sync, and recommendations.
functionalRequirements: Subscribe to a podcast show to get new episode notifications
Stream or download an episode for offline playback
Resume playback from the last position, synced across devices
Adjust playback speed
Auto-download new episodes for subscribed shows
Recommend shows based on listening history
nonFunctionalRequirements: Playback position sync across devices within a few seconds
Support millions of episodes and concurrent streams
hints: Core entities: Show, Episode, Subscription, PlaybackState (userId, episodeId, positionSeconds, updatedAt), Download. Store PlaybackState server-side, upserted on a debounced timer (e.g. every 10s) during playback, not on every second.
Cross-device sync: when a device resumes an episode, fetch the latest PlaybackState by updatedAt (last-write-wins) — simple and sufficient since a user typically listens on one device at a time.

New-episode notifications: use a fan-out-on-write model for subscriptions with a reasonable subscriber count (notify all subscribers when an episode publishes) versus fan-out-on-read for shows with huge subscriber counts (compute "any new episodes" lazily when the user opens the app).

title: Cloud File Sync Client (Dropbox-like)
description: Design the client-side sync engine for a cloud storage service that keeps local and remote folders in sync, handling conflicts.
functionalRequirements: Detect local file changes (create, edit, delete, move)
Upload changed files to the cloud and download remote changes locally
Chunk large files for efficient partial re-upload on edit
Detect and resolve sync conflicts (same file edited on two devices)
Support selective sync (only sync chosen folders)
Show sync status per file (syncing, synced, conflict, error)
nonFunctionalRequirements: Only re-upload changed chunks, not the whole file, on edits
Sync engine must survive process crashes without losing track of pending changes
hints: Core entities: FileMetadata (path, hash, version, modifiedTime), Chunk, SyncQueue, ConflictRecord. Split files into fixed-size or content-defined chunks and hash each one — on edit, only chunks whose hash changed need re-upload.
Use a local persistent journal/queue of pending changes (append-only log on disk) so if the client crashes mid-sync, it can resume from the journal instead of re-scanning the entire file tree.

Conflict detection: track a version number (or vector clock) per file. If local and remote versions have both advanced independently since the last common sync point, it's a conflict — resolve by keeping both as "file.txt" and "file (conflicted copy).txt" rather than silently overwriting.

title: Recipe & Meal Planning App
description: Design an app for browsing recipes, planning weekly meals, and auto-generating a shopping list.
functionalRequirements: Browse and search recipes by ingredient, cuisine, or dietary tag
Add a recipe to a weekly meal plan calendar
Scale recipe ingredient quantities based on serving size
Auto-generate a consolidated shopping list from a week's meal plan
Mark shopping list items as purchased
Save favorite recipes
nonFunctionalRequirements: Shopping list generation should merge duplicate ingredients across recipes
Search should return results in under 500ms
hints: Core entities: Recipe (ingredients with quantity+unit), MealPlan (date → Recipe), ShoppingList, Ingredient. Normalize ingredient units (e.g. convert tsp/tbsp/cup to a common base) so quantities can be merged correctly.

Shopping list generation: iterate all recipes in the meal plan, scale each ingredient by the plan's chosen serving multiplier, group by normalized ingredient name + unit, and sum quantities into one consolidated line item.

For search, build an inverted index over ingredient names, cuisine tags, and dietary tags so multi-filter queries (e.g. "vegetarian" AND "Italian") are a fast set intersection rather than a full scan.

title: Fitness Tracker App
description: Design a fitness tracking app that logs workouts, steps, and goals, and computes progress analytics.
functionalRequirements: Log workouts (type, duration, calories, distance)
Track daily step count and active minutes
Set fitness goals (weekly steps, weight target) and track progress
Show historical trends (weekly/monthly charts)
Award achievement badges for milestones
Sync data from wearable devices
nonFunctionalRequirements: Ingest sensor data streams without data loss
Support millions of daily active users logging data continuously
hints: Core entities: User, Workout, DailyActivity (steps, activeMinutes, date), Goal, Achievement. Store DailyActivity as one row per user per day, updated incrementally as new step-count events arrive from the device.

For trend charts, pre-aggregate DailyActivity into weekly/monthly rollups on a scheduled job rather than summing raw daily rows on every dashboard load — classic write-time vs read-time aggregation trade-off.

Achievements: model as a rule engine — each Achievement has a trigger condition (e.g. "7-day step streak >= 10k") evaluated against the user's recent DailyActivity whenever new data lands; award once and never re-evaluate a completed achievement.

title: Multiplayer Tic-Tac-Toe with Matchmaking
description: Design a real-time multiplayer Tic-Tac-Toe game with matchmaking, live moves, and rematches.
functionalRequirements: Match two waiting players into a new game session
Broadcast each move to both players in real time
Validate moves server-side (correct turn, empty cell)
Detect win, loss, and draw conditions
Support a rematch request between the same two players
Handle a player disconnecting mid-game
nonFunctionalRequirements: Move broadcast latency under 200ms
Support thousands of concurrent game sessions
hints: Core entities: MatchmakingQueue, GameSession, Board, Player, Move. Matchmaking is simply a FIFO queue — pop two waiting players and create a GameSession as soon as two are available.
Server is authoritative: every Move request is validated against the current Board and whose turn it is before being applied and broadcast — never trust a client-reported win/loss.
Win detection after each move only needs to check the row/column/diagonal through the just-played cell (not the whole board) — O(1) instead of scanning all 8 winning lines every time.

title: Elevator Group Control System (Multiple Elevators)
description: Design a control system that dispatches the optimal elevator among several to serve a hall call, minimizing wait time.
functionalRequirements: Handle hall calls (up/down) from any floor
Handle in-cabin floor requests from passengers
Dispatch the best elevator among N cars for a new hall call
Support elevator states: idle, moving up, moving down, door open
Batch requests along an elevator's current direction (SCAN-like)
Handle an elevator going out of service
nonFunctionalRequirements: Dispatch decision should compute in well under 100ms
Minimize average passenger wait time across the building
hints: Core entities: ElevatorController (dispatcher), Elevator (state, currentFloor, direction, requestQueue), HallCall, CabinRequest. Each Elevator maintains its own SCAN-ordered request queue (like a disk-scheduling elevator algorithm), serving requests in the current direction before reversing.

Dispatch heuristic: for a new hall call, score each idle/moving elevator by estimated time-to-arrival (distance, current direction alignment, number of pending stops) and assign the lowest-cost one — this is the crux of the classic "elevator group control" problem.

Model each elevator as its own state machine (Idle ⇄ MovingUp ⇄ MovingDown ⇄ DoorOpen) driven independently, with the ElevatorController only responsible for assigning calls, not micromanaging individual elevator movement.

title: Online Polling / Voting Platform
description: Design a platform for creating polls and collecting votes at scale, with real-time result aggregation and fraud prevention.
functionalRequirements: Create a poll with multiple options and an optional end time
Cast a single vote per user per poll
Show live-updating vote counts and percentages
Prevent duplicate voting (same user, same poll)
Support anonymous vs. authenticated polls
Close a poll and lock in final results
nonFunctionalRequirements: Vote counting must be accurate under massive concurrent write load
Result display can be eventually consistent (few-second lag acceptable)
hints: Core entities: Poll, Option, Vote (userId, pollId, optionId, unique together). Enforce one-vote-per-user with a unique index on (pollId, userId) at the database level — this is the real duplicate-vote guard, not just an application check.

For hot polls with huge write volume, don't increment a shared counter row directly (contention bottleneck) — instead write append-only Vote records and maintain per-option counters via a sharded counter or a stream-processing aggregator that batches increments.

Live result display: push aggregated counts to clients via WebSocket on a throttled interval (e.g. every 1-2 seconds) computed from the sharded counters, rather than recomputing from all raw Vote rows on every poll.

title: Warehouse Order Fulfillment System
description: Design a warehouse management system that picks, packs, and ships customer orders from inventory across multiple bins.
functionalRequirements: Track inventory quantity per SKU across multiple warehouse bins
Allocate inventory to an order at checkout time
Generate an optimized pick list/path for warehouse staff
Pack items into shipment boxes based on size/weight
Update order status: allocated, picking, packed, shipped
Handle partial fulfillment when stock is insufficient
nonFunctionalRequirements: Inventory allocation must never oversell available stock
Support thousands of orders processed per hour
hints: Core entities: SKU, Bin, InventoryRecord (SKU, bin, quantity), Order, Allocation, PickList. Allocation should atomically decrement available quantity (reserve) at checkout time — use optimistic locking or a DB transaction to avoid overselling under concurrent checkouts.

Pick list optimization: given a set of allocated bins for an order, sort the picks by warehouse layout position (e.g. serpentine aisle order) so staff walk a near-optimal path instead of jumping randomly between aisles.

Partial fulfillment: if total available quantity across bins is less than ordered quantity, split the order into a fulfilled sub-shipment and a backorder for the remainder, tracked as separate fulfillment records against the same parent Order.

title: Customer Support Ticketing System
description: Design a support ticketing system (like Zendesk) handling ticket creation, assignment, SLA tracking, and escalation.
functionalRequirements: Create a support ticket from a customer inquiry
Auto-assign or manually assign a ticket to an agent
Track ticket status: open, in-progress, waiting, resolved, closed
Set priority and SLA deadlines per ticket
Escalate a ticket that's about to breach its SLA
Support internal notes and customer-visible replies on a ticket
nonFunctionalRequirements: SLA breach detection must run reliably even under system load
Support tens of thousands of open tickets per organization
hints: Core entities: Ticket (status, priority, SLA deadline), Agent, Reply (internal vs public), EscalationRule. Model ticket status as a State Machine with allowed transitions (Open → InProgress → Waiting → Resolved → Closed, with Reopen from Closed).

SLA deadlines are computed at ticket creation/priority-change time (createdAt + SLA duration for that priority) and stored directly on the ticket — a scheduled job periodically scans tickets nearing/past deadline rather than computing deadlines on every check.

Auto-assignment: use round-robin or least-loaded-agent routing, factoring in agent skill tags matching the ticket's category — a simple weighted queue rather than a full ML system covers most real designs at this scope.

title: Loyalty Points & Rewards Program
description: Design a loyalty program that earns points on purchases, tracks tiers, and lets users redeem rewards.
functionalRequirements: Earn points on qualifying purchases based on configurable rules
Track a member's point balance and lifetime spend
Assign membership tiers (Silver/Gold/Platinum) based on activity
Redeem points for rewards (discounts, free items)
Expire points after a period of inactivity
Show point-earning history and upcoming tier progress
nonFunctionalRequirements: Point balance updates must be atomic and auditable
Support millions of members with concurrent earn/redeem operations
hints: Core entities: Member, PointsLedger (append-only entries: earn/redeem/expire), EarningRule, Tier, Reward. Never store a single mutable "balance" field as the source of truth — derive it from summing the PointsLedger, cached for fast reads.

Use a Rules Engine / Strategy pattern for earning: each EarningRule (e.g. "1 point per $1", "2x points on weekends") evaluates a purchase and returns points to award — new promotions become new rules, not new code paths.

Tier evaluation runs periodically (e.g. nightly) over each member's trailing 12-month spend/points, comparing against tier thresholds — avoid recalculating tier on every single transaction for performance.

title: Social Event Planning App (Meetup-like)
description: Design an app for creating and discovering local social events, with RSVPs, groups, and recommendations.
functionalRequirements: Create a group around a shared interest
Create an event under a group with date, location, and capacity
RSVP to an event (going, maybe, not going)
Discover nearby events based on user location and interests
Waitlist attendees once an event reaches capacity
Send event reminders to RSVP'd attendees
nonFunctionalRequirements: Nearby-event search should respond in under 300ms
Support millions of groups and events globally
hints: Core entities: Group, Event (location, capacity, startTime), RSVP, Member, Interest. Index event locations geospatially (geohash or a geo-index like PostGIS/Elasticsearch) for fast "events near me" queries.

Capacity + waitlist follows the same reserve-atomically-then-waitlist-on-full pattern used elsewhere (gym classes, e-book loans): an atomic increment-if-under-capacity on RSVP, FIFO waitlist otherwise.

Recommendations: score events by a simple weighted combination of interest-tag overlap with the user's followed Groups/Interests and physical distance, re-ranked and cached per user on a schedule rather than computed live on every page load.

title: Airline Management System
description: Design an airline management system that handles aircraft fleet management, flight scheduling, passenger seat reservation with conflict-free booking, crew assignment, check-in, and boarding pass generation.
functionalRequirements: Manage a fleet of aircraft with different seat configurations (Economy, Business, First Class)
Schedule flights with route, departure/arrival times, and aircraft assignment
Search available flights by origin, destination, and date
Book seats for passengers with seat selection; prevent double-booking
Handle booking cancellation and seat release with refund policy
Check-in passengers within the check-in window and generate boarding passes
Assign crew members (pilots, cabin crew) to flights respecting duty-hour limits
Track flight status: SCHEDULED → CHECK_IN_OPEN → BOARDING → DEPARTED → LANDED → COMPLETED (or CANCELLED/DELAYED)
nonFunctionalRequirements: Seat booking is atomic — concurrent requests for the last seat must not double-book
Flight search returns results in under 2 seconds for up to 500 flights/day
Crew assignment respects regulatory duty-hour limits without manual checks

title: Restaurant Management System
description: Design a comprehensive restaurant management system that covers menu and inventory management, table assignments, order processing with kitchen workflow, billing with tax and discount support, and table reservations.
functionalRequirements: Manage menu with categories, items, prices, and real-time availability toggles
Assign tables to walk-in or reserved customers based on capacity
Take orders for dine-in, takeaway, and delivery channels
Route order tickets to kitchen display system (KDS) upon placement
Track order status: PLACED → PREPARING → READY → SERVED
Generate itemised bills with tax, service charge, and promotional discounts
Manage ingredient inventory and flag low-stock items automatically
Accept table reservations with date, time-slot, and party-size validation
nonFunctionalRequirements: Order placement to kitchen notification in under 1 second
Support 50+ concurrent occupied tables without performance degradation
Bill generation (with all decorators applied) completes within 500ms

title: Distributed Rate Limiter (Multi-Node)
description: Design a rate limiter that enforces a consistent request limit for a client across many API server instances.
functionalRequirements: Enforce a limit like "100 requests per minute per API key" globally, not per-server
Support multiple algorithms: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket
Allow per-client custom limits/tiers
Return remaining quota and reset time to the client
Gracefully degrade if the central rate-limit store becomes unavailable
nonFunctionalRequirements: Rate-limit check latency should add well under 5ms to each request
Must work correctly across hundreds of stateless API server instances
Should tolerate the rate-limit store being briefly unavailable without blocking all traffic
hints: Because request limits must hold across many stateless servers, per-process in-memory counters don't work — use a shared fast store (Redis) as the single source of truth for counters, since local server memory can't coordinate globally.

Sliding window log or sliding window counter in Redis: use INCR with an expiring key per (clientId, windowStart) for fixed windows, or a sorted set of request timestamps trimmed to the window for a precise sliding log — token bucket can be implemented with a Lua script in Redis for atomicity (check-and-decrement in one round trip).

For resilience, if Redis is unreachable, fail open with a conservative local fallback limiter (e.g. each node allows a small fraction of the global limit) rather than rejecting all traffic — document this trade-off explicitly as availability over strict correctness during outages.

title: News Feed Ranking System
description: Design the backend for a social network news feed that aggregates and ranks posts from friends/follows at massive scale.
functionalRequirements: Aggregate posts from all accounts a user follows into one feed
Rank feed items by relevance (not strictly chronological)
Support near-real-time insertion of new posts into feeds
Handle both regular users and celebrities with millions of followers
Paginate the feed efficiently as the user scrolls
Exclude posts the user has already seen or hidden
nonFunctionalRequirements: Feed load latency under 200ms for a typical user
Support hundreds of millions of users, billions of posts
System must handle extreme fan-out for celebrity accounts without falling over
hints: Use a hybrid fan-out strategy: fan-out-on-write (push a new post into each follower's precomputed feed, stored e.g. in Redis lists) for regular users with a normal follower count, but fan-out-on-read (merge celebrity posts into the feed at read time instead of writing to millions of follower feeds) for accounts with huge followings — this avoids the "celebrity write storm" problem.

Ranking: compute a relevance score per candidate post (recency decay, affinity between user and poster, engagement signals) — do a first-pass candidate retrieval (recent posts from followed accounts, capped at a few hundred) then rank that smaller candidate set rather than scoring every post in the system.

Feed pagination: since the feed is dynamically ranked and merges multiple sources (precomputed pushed feed + live celebrity posts), use a cursor based on a composite (score, postId, timestamp) rather than simple offset pagination, so new posts arriving don't shift already-seen pages.

title: Distributed Job Scheduler (Airflow-like)
description: Design a distributed system for scheduling and executing DAGs of interdependent jobs across a cluster of workers.
functionalRequirements: Define a job as a DAG of tasks with dependencies
Schedule DAG runs on a cron-like or event-triggered basis
Execute tasks on any available worker in a cluster, respecting dependency order
Retry failed tasks with backoff, and support manual re-runs
Track task/DAG run status and provide a monitoring view
Prevent the same task instance from running twice concurrently
nonFunctionalRequirements: Must survive scheduler node failure without losing or duplicating DAG runs
Support thousands of DAGs with tens of thousands of tasks scheduled per day
Task dispatch latency under a few seconds once dependencies are satisfied
hints: Core entities: DAG (tasks + dependency edges), DAGRun (one execution instance), TaskInstance (status per task per run), Worker. Persist DAGRun/TaskInstance state in a database — the scheduler process itself must be stateless/recoverable, deriving all decisions by querying persisted state, not in-memory data.

Use a leader-election scheme (e.g. via Zookeeper/etcd) so exactly one scheduler instance is actively assigning tasks at a time, with standby instances ready to take over on failure — this avoids duplicate scheduling from multiple active schedulers.

Task dispatch: workers pull ready tasks (all dependencies SUCCESS) from a shared queue rather than the scheduler pushing directly, using a distributed lock or a claim-with-lease pattern (worker claims a task with a lease; if it dies mid-execution, the lease expires and another worker can reclaim it) to guarantee exactly-once execution semantics.

title: Distributed Notification Fanout System
description: Design a system that reliably delivers notifications (push, SMS, email) to millions of users with dedup, retries, and prioritization.
functionalRequirements: Accept a notification request targeting a user, group, or topic subscribers
Fan out a topic notification to all its subscribers
Deliver via multiple channels (push, SMS, email) based on user preference
Deduplicate identical notifications sent in a short window
Retry failed deliveries with backoff and respect provider rate limits
Support notification priority (critical vs. marketing)
nonFunctionalRequirements: Deliver critical notifications within seconds even under heavy load
Support fanning out to tens of millions of subscribers for a single topic event
At-least-once delivery guarantee with idempotent handling on the client
hints: Core pipeline: Ingestion API → durable Message Queue (e.g. Kafka) → Fanout workers that expand a topic notification into per-user delivery tasks → per-channel Delivery workers (Push/SMS/Email) that call the respective provider APIs. Decoupling each stage with a queue lets you scale and retry independently.

Deduplication: assign each notification (or the (userId, templateId, dedupeWindow) tuple) an idempotency/dedupe key, checked against a short-TTL cache (Redis) before enqueueing delivery — this prevents duplicate sends from retries or overlapping triggers.

Priority and rate-limit handling: use separate queues per priority tier (critical vs. marketing) so critical notifications aren't stuck behind a backlog of bulk marketing sends, and apply a token-bucket limiter per downstream provider (APNs/FCM/Twilio) so a burst doesn't get the whole account throttled or banned by the provider.

title: Content Delivery Network (CDN)
description: Design a CDN that caches and serves static content from edge locations close to users, with origin fetch and cache invalidation.
functionalRequirements: Route a user request to the nearest/best edge server
Serve cached content from the edge if available (cache hit)
Fetch from origin on a cache miss and populate the edge cache
Support cache invalidation/purge for updated content
Support configurable TTLs per content type
Provide cache-hit-ratio and traffic analytics
nonFunctionalRequirements: Cache hit latency under 20ms from edge
Support petabytes of cacheable content across thousands of edge nodes globally
High availability — an edge node failure shouldn't cause origin overload
hints: Routing to the nearest edge is typically done via DNS-based geo-routing (Anycast IP or GeoDNS resolving to the closest edge PoP) so the client's first request already lands near them without any application-level logic.

Each edge node runs its own local cache (keyed by URL + relevant headers, e.g. Vary: Accept-Encoding) with an LRU/LFU eviction policy; on a miss, the edge does a "cache-fill" request to a regional/origin tier rather than every edge node hitting origin directly — a mid-tier cache layer protects the origin from thundering-herd traffic.

Invalidation at scale: rather than pushing a purge to every one of thousands of edges synchronously (slow, unreliable), use a versioned cache key (embed a content version/hash in the cache key) so publishing new content is just a new key — old cached versions simply expire via TTL and are never served again, avoiding a distributed invalidation problem entirely for immutable-content workloads. For mutable paths, maintain a purge queue consumed asynchronously by edges.

title: Distributed Lock Manager (Zookeeper-like)
description: Design a distributed coordination service that provides mutual exclusion locks and leader election across a cluster of nodes.
functionalRequirements: Acquire and release a named distributed lock
Support blocking acquire (wait until available) and try-acquire (fail fast)
Automatically release a lock if the holder crashes (no permanent deadlock)
Support leader election among a group of competing nodes
Notify waiters when a lock becomes available or leadership changes
Ensure at most one holder of a given lock at any time cluster-wide
nonFunctionalRequirements: The lock service itself must be fault-tolerant (survive minority node failures)
Lock state must be strongly consistent — no split-brain with two simultaneous holders
Failover/re-election should complete within a few seconds of a leader failure
hints: The lock service's own data (who holds which lock) must be replicated via a consensus protocol like Raft or Paxos across an odd number of nodes (e.g. 3 or 5), so it keeps functioning correctly as long as a majority quorum is alive — this is what makes the coordinator itself fault-tolerant and split-brain-proof.

A classic implementation pattern (as in ZooKeeper): create an ephemeral, sequentially-numbered node under a lock path when a client wants the lock; the client holding the lowest-numbered node holds the lock, and each other waiter watches the node just before its own — when that node is deleted (released or the holder's session expires), the next waiter is notified.

Crash recovery: bind the lock to the client's session (a heartbeat-based liveness lease) — if the holder's session/heartbeat times out (crash, network partition), the coordinator automatically deletes its ephemeral lock node, releasing the lock to the next waiter without requiring any manual intervention.

title: Live Video Streaming Platform (Twitch-like)
description: Design a platform for low-latency live video broadcasting from a streamer to potentially millions of concurrent viewers.
functionalRequirements: Ingest a live video stream from a broadcaster
Transcode the stream into multiple quality/bitrate renditions
Distribute the live stream to potentially millions of concurrent viewers
Support adaptive bitrate streaming based on viewer bandwidth
Provide live chat alongside the stream
Support stream recording/VOD for later playback
nonFunctionalRequirements: End-to-end latency (broadcaster to viewer) as low as a few seconds
Support a single stream scaling to millions of concurrent viewers
Graceful quality degradation under network congestion, not buffering/failure
hints: Pipeline: Broadcaster encodes and pushes via RTMP/WebRTC to an Ingest server → Transcoding service produces multiple bitrate renditions (e.g. via HLS/DASH segments) → segments are pushed to a CDN/edge network → viewers pull segments from the nearest edge, not from the origin ingest server, which is what allows scaling to millions of viewers.

Adaptive bitrate: the player periodically measures download throughput and switches between available renditions (manifest lists multiple quality variants) — this is a client-side decision, the server just needs to have produced and published all the bitrate variants as short segments (a few seconds each).

Latency vs. scale trade-off: shorter segment durations reduce latency but increase overhead (more requests, harder to cache efficiently) — protocols like Low-Latency HLS/DASH or WebRTC-based fan-out trees are used specifically to push latency down from the traditional ~30s of HLS to a few seconds while still using a CDN for the actual fan-out to viewers.
